```{r setup_poster, include=FALSE}
library(targets)
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)

tar_source(here::here("R")) # One plot needs a custom function
tar_config_set(store = here::here("_targets"))
tar_load(questions)
tar_load(summaries_correctness_by_model)
tar_load(n_replications)

n_questions <- nrow(questions)
n_models <- summaries_correctness_by_model |> distinct(model_id) |> nrow()

best <- summaries_correctness_by_model |> arrange(desc(.prob)) |> slice(1)
best_acc <- scales::percent(best$.prob, accuracy = 0.1)
best_model <- best$model_id
```

## Row {.content-row height=max-content}

::: {.card title="Introduction"}

Large language models (LLMs) now approach professional-level performance on medical MCQs.

Travel medicine is dynamic and under-studied: region-specific risks and evolving recommendations.

We benchmarked diverse models and prompting strategies on single-best-answer questions.

:::

::: {.card title="Methods"}

**Questions**: 42 travel-medicine items (single correct option out of four).

**Models**: Frontier, hosted open-source, and local quantised replicas.

**Prompt strategies**: "cold" (answer only), "free" (brief rationale + answer), and "reasoning" (CoT).

**Replications**: 5 per (item, model, prompt) cell to assess variability.

**Metrics**: Accuracy, parsability (output format adherence), consistency (replication stability).

**Bayesian modelling**: Hierarchical models to model model impact adjusted for items and prompt strategies.

:::

::: {.card title="Results"}

**Reasoning models** (e.g., o3, Gemini 2.5 Pro) led the benchmark, especially if equipped with **internet search capabilities** (e.g., Sonar Reasoning).

**Local or low-parameter count models** performed worst.

**Prompting strategies had modest impact** at the top end; model class mattered more.

:::
